item.title: Implement safe_extract.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, verbatim): "Implement `safe_extract.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Repository: quality-safe-extract. Read SPEC.md first and treat it as the authoritative contract. Preserve the documented public API exactly. Implement every specified error type and boundary case. Extend the existing tests with focused tests covering each specified error and boundary case; do not weaken or delete existing tests. Use only the Python standard library. Keep functions under 60 lines and follow the repository's existing style. Commit the work on the local branch (ship mode is local; do not push).

Security-sensitive: archive extraction must reject path traversal, absolute paths, and links that escape the destination, as SPEC.md specifies. Verify the test suite passes before finishing and report the exact command and result.

reasons: sizer: critical -> x_high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier

evidence.caption: Final test run at cbf3a91: 32 tests, all pass. No before/after comparison because the base is a NotImplementedError stub.

pr.body: Approach: extract() runs _check_batch, _check_root and per-target _check_target_free over the entire batch before the first write. Target checks use os.lstat and treat only FileNotFoundError as absent, so validation-time I/O errors propagate and nothing is written. Files are opened with 'xb', so existing files are never overwritten. Entries must be (name, data) tuples; lists are rejected as malformed, a reading of the spec's 'tuples' wording. Key files: safe_extract.py, test_safe_extract.py. Checks: `python3 -m unittest -v test_safe_extract`, 32 tests OK at cbf3a91. Review: review-1 (fail, fixed in cbf3a91), review-2 (pass on 541394d), review-3 (fail, fixed in cbf3a91), review-delta-4 (pass on cbf3a91). Advisory follow-ups, left open: a mid-write I/O error (ENOSPC, EIO) can leave earlier files and a partial file; SPEC puts rollback out of scope, and the docstring should say so. Tests create temp dirs in cwd (existing repo style). No NUL-only test. The 'xb' race guard is untested. Limits: tests run as root in the sandbox, so permission-based tests use a mocked os.lstat instead of chmod.
pr.summary: Implemented safe_extract.extract per SPEC.md. Before: NotImplementedError stub with 2 basic tests. Now: whole-batch validation before any write (shape, names, duplicates, file/dir collisions, root, symlinks, existing targets), exclusive-create writes, 32 tests covering each specified error and boundary.
pr.title: feat: implement safe_extract.extract per SPEC

risk.why: Security and file-writing safety: the change decides whether writes below a caller-supplied root may begin, and enforces symlink-escape, traversal and no-overwrite rules. Reviewers returned high. Behaviour is new, and tests cover each specified error and boundary, including the validation-time I/O path fixed in cbf3a91.
